title: The Garden That Closes
mathematical_role: Exhibit one exact finite union-closed family and make closure plus the global frequency question visible.
learning_objective: Read an explicit family, verify selected unions and exact cover relations, and compare element frequencies with the half threshold without mistaking one example for a proof of the general conjecture.
literal_semantics: F = {∅,{a},{b},{a,b},{a,c},{a,b,c}} is the finite family depicted.
The seven displayed inclusion edges are exactly the cover relations of the depicted family.
nonliteral_semantics: Node spacing and edge geometry do not encode metric or probabilistic information.

notes: Exact finite-example data and cover relations are reproduced by governed tests.
Imported theorem-terrain language remains bounded by the documentary source and does not admit a new external claim.

accessibility.alt_text: Exact six-set union-closed family shown as a strict Hasse-style cover diagram, with frequencies a in four sets, b in three, c in two, and half threshold three.
accessibility.long_description: The plate depicts F={∅,{a},{b},{a,b},{a,c},{a,b,c}} with exactly its seven inclusion cover relations. Selected unions are written explicitly. A frequency ledger gives counts 4, 3, and 2 for a, b, and c; because |F|=6, the half threshold is 3, so a exceeds and b meets it in this example. The caption distinguishes this exact example from Frankl's general conjecture and states the conjecture only for finite union-closed families with at least one nonempty member.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: For the explicitly displayed six-set family, the shown seven cover relations, selected unions, frequencies, and half threshold are exact.
not_claimed: Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture in general
A classification of all union-closed families
Any metric, probabilistic, or geometric meaning in node spacing

supersession_reason: R2 preserves the exact six-set example while correcting glyph robustness, Hasse-cover ambiguity, threshold wording, selected-union framing, and the literal scope of the Frankl caption.
